title: Run start blocks the UI thread on per-host Vault and credential resolution — and deadlocks permanently on a cold Vault cache
existing_state: All run entry points materialize host connections synchronously on the UI thread before any await: ExecutePresetOnRowsAsync calls GetHostConnections(hostRows).ToList() at Form1.cs:12277, the folder path at Form1.cs:12900, and the parallel connection test reaches it too at Form1.cs:8916 (the SemaphoreSlim(5).WaitAsync at 8910-8913 completes synchronously for the first 5 rows, so the lambda keeps running on the UI thread). Inside the per-row iterator (Form1.cs:13309-13391), every row with a vault_path calls VaultCredentialProvider.TryGetPassword, which blocks via .GetAwaiter().GetResult() on VaultService.ReadSecretKeysAsync (Services/Vault/VaultCredentialProvider.cs:48-49). VaultService.cs contains zero ConfigureAwait(false) (verified by grep — only VaultOidcLoginFlow has them), so on any cache miss the first real await (e.g. HttpClient.SendAsync during auth at VaultService.cs:323) posts its continuation back to the blocked WindowsFormsSynchronizationContext — a permanent sync-over-async deadlock, not just a slow call. The 300s instance cache (VaultService.cs:1065) is shared with background script/job runs (which execute under Task.Run, SshExecutionService.cs:446), masking the bug: a UI run works right after a background run warmed the cache and hangs otherwise. Even with the deadlock fixed, resolution is one sequential HTTPS round-trip per row (a cold 200-host fleet = 200 round-trips with the form frozen and no progress or cancel), an expired OIDC token launches the full browser login flow (VaultService.cs:448-573, up to 180s) inside the blocking call, and there is no single-flight gate around authentication (GetAuthenticatedProfileAsync, VaultService.cs:282-313 has no lock), so parallel callers with an expired token each perform a full login. The same enumeration also performs a Credential Manager CredWrite syscall per row with a grid password as a side effect (StoreHostPassword, Form1.cs:13349-13352) or a CredRead fallback (13353-13356).
recommendation: Make host-credential resolution genuinely async: snapshot the grid cell values on the UI thread (cheap), then resolve credentials in an awaited background task before SetExecutionMode(true) — extract an async ResolveHostConnectionsAsync and await it in ExecutePresetOnRowsAsync / ExecuteFolderWithOptionsAsync / the connection-test path (the callers are already async Task; Task.Run around the vault batch is an acceptable first step). Dedupe distinct vault_path values and resolve them concurrently with a small cap (e.g. SemaphoreSlim(4)) behind a cancellable progress UI. Add an async TryGetPasswordAsync to VaultCredentialProvider so the sync-over-async bridge disappears from this path; add ConfigureAwait(false) throughout VaultService as defense-in-depth; add a per-profile single-flight SemaphoreSlim around GetAuthenticatedProfileAsync so concurrent resolution cannot trigger N simultaneous logins or N OIDC browser windows fighting over the callback port. Move the StoreHostPassword CredWrite side effect out of enumeration to the explicit save path, keeping only TryResolveHostPassword reads here.
user_benefit: The app stops hard-freezing — and in the cold-cache case permanently hanging — the moment Run is pressed on a grid using the vault_path column; the feature becomes usable from the UI at all, and large fleets resolve credentials in parallel with visible, cancellable progress instead of one blocking HTTPS call per host.
